subject: Negotiating SLO telemetry access for procurement review
raw_thread:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement and dashboard access

Markus,

Thanks for taking this through procurement. We're collecting answers for Acme's security and procurement board — a short set of questions below on how Redwood measures SLOs and what access we can get to metrics for the evaluation period. Please reply by EOD Tuesday if possible.

1) Single-line answers are fine: What are your standard SLOs for hosted API (availability and p50/p95 latency)? Measurement window and error budget calculation?
2) Where are these metrics sourced from (internal runtime telemetry, edge proxies, load balancer)?
3) Retention: how long do you keep raw telemetry and aggregated percentiles?
4) Alerting: what channels do you support (email, webhook, pager) and who is on-call for customer-impacting SLO breaches?
5) Customer access: can Acme get a read-only Grafana/dashboard for our org, and/or periodic exported CSVs of latency percentiles? Any conditions/approvals?
6) SOC2 / audit artifacts: how can we access the relevant reports or evidence?

Attachments: procurement_sow.docx (we've attached our standard questionnaire form).

Appreciate a short reply and a proposed time for a quick sync with your solutions engineer.

Thanks,
Sarah Lopez
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
procurement@acmecorp.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement and dashboard access

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'm attaching a compact "SLO evidence" spreadsheet that maps our runtime metrics to the procurement questions (slo_evidence_summary.xlsx). Happy to walk through on a short call.

1) Standard SLOs (hosted API): Availability: 99.95% over a 30d rolling window. Latency: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 350ms for generation endpoints (depending on model family and sequence length). Error budget calculated on rolling 30d windows.
2) Metrics source: primary telemetry is collected inside the serving runtime (request ingress, per-node request latency, kernel timings) and aggregated at the regional telemetry cluster. We also cross-validate with edge/load balancer metrics for network-level drops.
3) Retention: aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) retained for 365 days. Raw per-request traces/headers retained for 90 days and are available for audit on request (subject to redaction/PII rules).
4) Alerting: Email and webhook alerts are standard; we can also configure webhook integrations to your paging system (PagerDuty/opsgenie) for Sev2/Sev1 SLO breaches. Our on-call rotations are ops-led; for customer-impacting incidents we run runbooks that include an assigned CS/SE liaison.
5) Customer access: We can offer a filtered, read-only Grafana org view scoped to your account plus daily CSV exports for the evaluation period. Direct access requires a security review (standard MR) and an access agreement — in practice we typically provide read-only dashboards within 3 business days after procurement sign-off.
6) SOC2: We can share a SOC2 SOC-2 Type II summary and provide access to the full report via a secure Drive link after an NDA.

Next steps: I can loop in Aditya (solutions eng) to scope the demo and walk the team through the dashboard. Proposed times: Tue 12/1 10:00 or Wed 12/2 14:00 PT.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Attachment: slo_evidence_summary.xlsx

Sarah

Markus / Aditya — quick internal note. Acme's ask (read-only Grafana + nightly export) is consistent with our usual evaluation support. We should be able to approve a limited, scoped invitation without a full legal amendment, provided:

- The Grafana org is scoped to account-level only (no cross-customer data),
- Dashboards are restricted to aggregate latency/availability panels, no logs/traces,
- Exports are pre-filtered and stored under a secure S3 bucket with 90-day retention by default,
- Security team signs off on the webhook auth scheme (HMAC) before enabling webhooks.

If procurement needs SLA credit language, we have a standard clause we can propose (credit tiers based on monthly uptime percentage). If they ask for exceptions to our retentions beyond 365 days, that needs a legal amendment and potential storage-cost pass-through.

Approve for engineering to provision the read-only view and the nightly CSV for a 90-day evaluation period. Markus, please confirm and send the onboarding steps to Acme procurement.

Laura

Sarah — thanks for the follow-ups. Confirming and proposing a compromise we can operationally deliver quickly:

- Maintenance & exclusions: Scheduled maintenance >1 hour per-region is excluded from availability calculations; we publish a maintenance calendar and post-incident notes to the dashboard when a maintenance impacts SLOs. Regional failovers are evaluated in the post-incident review; we commit to transparent incident notes.
- Webhooks: Yes — we support authenticated webhooks with HMAC signatures and timestamp checking. We will share the signing key handshake and verification docs as part of onboarding.
- Nightly CSV exports: will include timestamped p50/p90/p95/p99 and total request counts per hour. Exports will be available to your secure S3 location for 90 days. If you need longer retention we can propose a paid extension.
- Grafana access: we'll provision a read-only Grafana org scoped to Acme with dashboards limited to latency and availability panels (no logs/traces). We'll include a short "onboarding document" with screenshots and an ACL map.
- SLA credit language: we'll propose our standard monthly uptime credit clause (credit tiers tied to monthly uptime buckets). I attached a short PDF with the onboarding steps and what to expect (grafana-invite-instructions.pdf).

Next step: Can you confirm the preferred S3 bucket and a point of contact for the security review? If it's easier, let's set up a 30-minute call with Aditya (solutions engineering) and one of your ops folks — we're available Tue 12/1 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
